findings.evidence: The new file declares `theorem mul_nonneg (i j : I) : 0 ≤ A i j * A j i` and `theorem mul_eq_zero_iff (i j : I) : A i j * A j i = 0 ↔ A i j = 0` inside `namespace IsGeneralizedCartan`, next to `protected theorem transpose` and `protected theorem submatrix`. Root `mul_nonneg` is Mathlib's ordered-semiring lemma. A grep finds no root `mul_eq_zero_iff`, but finds `theorem mul_eq_zero_iff` in Mathlib/Algebra/Tropical/Basic.lean:596 (namespace `Tropical`).
findings.fix: Declare both as `protected theorem mul_nonneg` and `protected theorem mul_eq_zero_iff`. The existing dot-notation uses (`hA.mul_nonneg`, `hA.mul_eq_zero_iff`) keep working.
findings.issue: `Matrix.IsGeneralizedCartan.mul_nonneg` reuses the name of Mathlib's root `mul_nonneg` and is not `protected`. Inside `namespace Matrix.IsGeneralizedCartan`, or under `open Matrix.IsGeneralizedCartan`, a bare `mul_nonneg` silently picks this lemma or becomes ambiguous. The sibling `transpose` and `submatrix` in the same file are already `protected`. `IsGeneralizedCartan.mul_eq_zero_iff` has the same defect, but only clashes with Mathlib's `Tropical.mul_eq_zero_iff` when `Tropical` is also open, because Mathlib has no root `mul_eq_zero_iff`.

summary: Names follow Mathlib conventions, and the dot-notation material is filed under the Mathlib types it extends (`Matrix`, `CoxeterSystem`, `CoxeterMatrix`, `DihedralGroup`, `MonoidHom`, `Polynomial.Chebyshev`, `CartanMatrix`). The one problem is that `Matrix.IsGeneralizedCartan.mul_nonneg` and `Matrix.IsGeneralizedCartan.mul_eq_zero_iff` are not `protected`, so they shadow root Mathlib lemmas (`mul_eq_zero_iff` only once Mathlib's `Tropical` namespace is also open).
